blocking_issues: Frontier-trend inference ignores selection on records. The frontier subset (frontier_subset() in run.py) keeps only models that raised the running-best accuracy, so its y-values are monotonically increasing BY CONSTRUCTION and P(beta>0)~1 is guaranteed regardless of any true trend; reviewer simulation under a pure null (beta=0, sigma_model=0.91, the real cybench fitted release dates) gives a mean record-subset OLS slope of +2.70 logits/yr with P(slope>0)=1.000 — the same order as the reported frontier velocity +3.11 [2.44, 3.74]. Yet FINDINGS quotes 'Frontier velocity +3.11 ... P>0 > 0.999' (finding 1), 'frontier +0.97 ... P>0=0.976' (finding 2), and headlines finding 3 with the frontier difference 'P = 0.9995'; the residual sigma estimated on a record-selected monotone subset is also biased downward, making those HDIs optimistic, and the beta2 saturation check (finding 6) inherits the same selection. The mean-trend results (the primary findings) are unaffected. Required fix (cheap): add an explicit record-selection caveat; stop presenting frontier P(beta>0) as evidence (drop or label as descriptive-by-construction); quote frontier slopes as descriptive record-path summaries; ideally add a synthetic-null check for the frontier estimator to quantify the artifact (analogous to the existing recovery suite), or replace the frontier fit with a selection-aware estimator (e.g., fit the trend + max over all models and derive the frontier from posterior predictive).
suggestions: Persist the verification numbers quoted in FINDINGS Data section to outputs/ ('298 eval_ids', '2-5 S3 locations', boolq max split difference 0.03): they are correct (reviewer reproduced 298, 2-5, 0.0321 from the parquet) but currently not traceable to any output file, which the traceability contract requires.

vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is excluded as 'cannot be dated', but Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct has a public release date (2024-07-23). Restate the exclusion reason as 'locally hosted checkpoint, weight provenance unverifiable' or include it; impact is immaterial (the 5 vllm rows total).

Consider noting that observing 7 records among 12 cybench models is itself informal evidence of a trend (expected ~3.1 under exchangeability) — a legitimate, selection-free frontier statistic that could partially replace the invalid frontier P-values.
